item.title: Onion price jumps 900% to N300,000 in 6 months
item.description: By Cynthia Alo The price of a 120kg bag of onions jumped from N30,000 in April 2026, to about N300,000 in October representing a 900 percent increase in six months. National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN) attributed the increase to inadequate storage facilities and fire outbreaks in warehouses in the North which contributed to post-harvest losses of more than 51 percent within the period. A Vanguard AgroBiz market survey shows that the price of a big sack of fresh onions at Mile 12 Lagos international market is N300,000, while the dried one is between N350,000 to N380,000 as of last week. In an interview with Vanguard AgroBiz, the National President of NOPPMAN, Aliyu Isah, said the price surge was not necessarily due to inadequate national production, but rather the loss of a significant proportion of harvested onions before the next production season. “It’s not that we did not produce enough for the country, but we lost more than 51% from April to October,” he said. Isah attributed the losses to poor storage facilities, fires that destroyed onions in local storage centres and the disruption caused by unsuitable seeds introduced into Nigeria during the 2024–2025 growing season. He said the seed, reportedly brought in from Algeria, was unsuitable for Nigeria’s farming system and caused substantial losses to farmers’ investments. According to him, the seed crisis alone resulted in losses estimated at nearly N100bn, while the sector needed government intervention to prevent the disruption from worsening into a supply shortage. He said government intervention was necessary when a crisis affected an agricultural subsector, warning that failure to address the underlying problems could deepen losses in subsequent seasons. Isah said the Ministry of Agriculture had discussed support for the onion subsector with the Bank of Agriculture and the Nigerian Agricultural Development Fund (NADF), regarding seed supply and farm inputs. He said the association had yet to receive the proposed intervention at the time of the interview, although discussions were ongoing. The support, he added, should help farmers restore production and prevent a repeat of the crisis. Looking ahead, Isah expects supplies from Sokoto to begin around November and December, followed by Aliero in Kebbi State from late December to January. The main harvest season is expected around March and April. He expressed optimism that the incoming harvest would ease prices, but said better storage facilities and timely government support were needed to reduce losses and prevent future shortages. item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil
item.description: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday. Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff election to Lula on Sunday, entered Argentina on Tuesday night before boarding a flight to Ecuador, the country’s National Directorate of Migration said on X. The 45-year-old entered Argentina “with valid travel documents and no legal impediment,” it added, despite a court order banning his exit. Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters boarded “a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador,” the government agency said. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. Baires Fly did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment. US media citing anonymous sources had earlier reported that Bolsonaro had arrived in the United States on Tuesday. The US State Department said it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family but did not confirm their travel plans. Brazil’s Supreme Court banned Bolsonaro from leaving the country and ordered him to hand over his passports. He is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity. Bolsonaro has not acknowledged his electoral defeat, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transport difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. item.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
item.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival’s opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election. Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack. Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority. After 51.8 percent of ballots were counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc had 49 seats and the Arab parties 16. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted. Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament. The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. The partial results suggest that Eisenkot’s bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties. But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 am (0100 GMT) on Wednesday morning, called for a “strong government of the right” and said the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped the premier “a lot”. – ‘Public voted for change’ – Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. item.title: Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation
item.description: Arsenal suffered a stunning League Cup fourth-round defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday. The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in one of the greatest shocks in the history of English football. AFP Sport looks at five other epic cup upsets: Wrexham 2 Arsenal 1 (1992 FA Cup) The previous season 90 places had separated the two clubs in the English Football League, with Arsenal having claimed their second title in three seasons under manager George Graham. Alan Smith put the Gunners in front, but Mickey Thomas’s free-kick levelled matters with 10 minutes remaining and Steve Watkin astonishingly claimed a late winner. Chelsea 2 Bradford 4 (2015 FA Cup) Chelsea won the FA Cup five times between 2006 and 2018, but Jose Mourinho’s Blues were humbled by third tier Bradford at Stamford Bridge. The Premier League leaders went 2-0 up through Gary Cahill and Ramires. But Bradford stormed back and goals from Jon Stead, Filipe Morais, Andy Halliday and Mark Yeates left Chelsea in tatters. Hereford 2 Newcastle 1 (1972 FA Cup) The fourth-round tie that had everything: pitch invasions by Parka-clad fans and Ronnie Radford scoring one of the FA Cup’s greatest FA Cup goals. Malcolm Macdonald put Newcastle ahead eight minutes from time and it seemed as if there would be no fairytale for the non-league outfit. But Radford equalised with a screamer from 25 yards and Ricky George won it for Hereford in extra-time. Liverpool 0 Wimbledon 1 (1988 FA Cup) Wimbledon’s ‘Crazy Gang’ were given no chance to stop Liverpool from claiming a league and cup double in the final at Wembley. Wimbledon had been a third-tier side four years earlier and Liverpool had won the title by a margin of nine points. But Lawrie Sanchez headed home from Dennis Wise’s free-kick before Wimbledon keeper Dave Beasant saved John Aldridge’s penalty to seal the upset. Grimsby 2 Manchester United 2, Grimsby won 12-11 on penalties (2025 League Cup) United trailed 2-0 as Grimsby duo Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren scored to expose the flaws in their supposedly superior opponents. Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire managed to take the second-round tie into extra-time. But Grimsby won on penalties to leave then-United boss Ruben Amorim shell-shocked. item.title: ‘A very sad day’: Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood
item.description: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal’s stunning League Cup defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood was “a very sad day” as the Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing results in their history. Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. The Gunners boss conceded Arsenal could have no complaints, admitting it was a painful moment in his reign. “First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day,” Arteta said. “There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. “The determination, you could see that was there from the start, even with 10 men. But we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum. “Obviously we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. “It’s football, that’s the beauty of this competition. It’s a very sad day.” Arsenal had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arteta’s team returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history. “Zero problem attitude-wise. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way,” Arteta said. “You don’t capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out.” – ‘I just can’t believe it’ – Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off. “Something that we discussed already before the match,” Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. “It’s difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation.” Fleetwood made a mockery of the 84 places between the clubs in the English football system with a defiant display that stopped Arsenal establishing any momentum. item.title: Nigerian extradited from Benin to US over alleged $100m tax fraud
item.description: A 43-year-old Nigerian, Akinade Adedeji Raheem, has been extradited from Benin to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged scheme involving more than $100 million in fraudulent tax refund claims using stolen identities. Raheem was arraigned in a US federal court following his extradition and ordered detained in the custody of the US Marshals Service pending further proceedings, according to the US Department of Justice. Prosecutors alleged that Raheem and his co-conspirators filed more than 300 fraudulent tax returns between 2018 and 2023, seeking over $100 million in refunds from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said the alleged operation involved hundreds of stolen identities and significant financial losses. “Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other locations,” Hertzberg said. “The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States,” he added. The indictment also named Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, as an alleged co-conspirator. Eletu was indicted separately and arrested in the UK, where extradition proceedings are pending. According to court documents, the suspects allegedly obtained the personal information of American taxpayers and tax professionals, including names, addresses and Social Security numbers, to facilitate fraudulent claims. Investigators said the alleged scheme involved creating online IRS accounts to access private taxpayer information, filing false returns and directing refunds to prepaid debit cards linked to addresses controlled by the suspects. Prosecutors further alleged that Raheem, Eletu and others laundered some of the proceeds by purchasing money orders in amounts intended to avoid reporting requirements. The money was allegedly used to acquire used cars through auction platforms, some of which were shipped to Nigeria, as well as designer clothing and other items. Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr. of the IRS Criminal Investigation Texas Field Office said the alleged scheme affected hundreds of taxpayers. “Raheem is an alleged co-conspirator in a nationwide identity theft scheme that victimised hundreds of taxpayers. The fraud also stole from the US Treasury, impacting programmes serving us all,” Altemus said. He added that authorities were working internationally to bring suspects in financial crimes to justice. “We are pursuing financial criminals to take back the stolen money and their freedom,” he said. item.title: French Senate passes bill to make protesters pay for unrest damage
item.description: The French parliament’s upper house passed a bill Wednesday that would make protesters financially liable for damage caused during street demonstrations, despite warnings from critics that it could curb the right to protest. The bill was drafted in response to riots that followed Paris Saint-Germain’s victory over Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League final in May. But it has taken on added significance after weeks of protests over inequality and soaring prices culminated in some of the worst violence France has seen in years on October 17, when thousands of businesses across the country were damaged and looted. The Senate passed an expanded version of the bill by 229 votes to 105, backed by a right-wing and centrist alliance which holds a majority. The legislation has been sent to the National Assembly, which is split between France’s political factions, for debate and voting. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, whom opinion polls place as the frontrunner to succeed Emmanuel Macron in next spring’s presidential election, supports the legislation. Speaking in parliament, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stressed the “urgency” of responding to the damage and scenes of chaos seen on October 17. “We can no longer allow the vast majority of our fellow citizens to pay for a minority of vandals,” he said. – ‘Legal travesty’ – Under the legislation, protesters could be ordered to pay up to 10,000 euros for damage caused during street demonstrations. But critics argue that people who took no part in vandalism could nonetheless be held liable if they were deemed to have been associated with those responsible. The bill introduces joint financial liability for anyone found to have “knowingly participated” in a group formed with the intent of carrying out acts of vandalism. It would also apply to individuals who “voluntarily” continued to take part in a gathering likely to disrupt public order after two police dispersal warnings. Welfare benefits and housing assistance could also be seized to help cover the cost of damages under the scheme, a provision that has drawn sharp criticism from left-wing parties and advocacy groups. In the second reading, senators toughened the measure to include other social benefits such as the family supplement, back-to-school allowance and the employment bonus. Left-wing lawmakers accused the government of an “authoritarian drift” at the expense of the freedom to demonstrate. Communist senator Fabien Gay denounced what he called a “legal travesty that deliberately conflates protesters and rioters”. Green senator Melanie Vogel accused the government of responding to social demands with “collective punishment.” Supporters of the bill sought to reassure critics. “We must not give the impression that this bill would criminalise a passer-by or a peaceful protester,” said Olivier Bitz of the centre-right Horizons party. – ‘Disastrous consequences’ – The government has proposed introducing protest bans targeting the most violent individuals

item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters? item.title: Trump says Putin-Zelensky meeting to be set up ‘very soon’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky would be set up “very soon.” The announcement came as Trump’s administration ramps up diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year. “There’ll be a meeting set up very soon and I think a lot of progress could be made,” Trump told reporters. Zelensky said on Sunday that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November, aiming to restart stalled peace talks. The Kremlin had previously said that a meeting between the three countries was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November. Putin, who ordered the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine. Trump came to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours — but over a year of US-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough, with tens of thousands killed. In recent days Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war. item.title: FG moves to secure farms, attract investors
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has moved to address insecurity threatening agricultural investments, signing a partnership agreement to develop security arrangements for farms and attract investors to multibillion-dollar soybean and sugarcane projects in Yobe and Jigawa states. The Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Integranium Holdings and Defence Agricultural Assets and Projects Development Company (DAPCO), supported by Defence Holding Company Limited, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abuja. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Dr Femi Ogunseinde, MOFI’s Executive Director, Investments, said: “We have a soybean initiative in Yobe, we have a sugarcane initiative in Jigawa—all large-scale, all multibillion-dollar projects. “Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.” He said the partnership would provide a platform to approach prospective investors with security arrangements designed to protect their investments. Also speaking, the Managing Director of MOFI, Dr Armstrong Takang, said: “Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export.” He said the partnership would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting public and private investment. On his part, DAPCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said: “The defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements.” He added that surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, while serving military personnel and veterans would also be considered. Ogunseinde said: “An estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of land could be available for farming, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production.” He added that the partners had identified several opportunities and expected at least one project to break ground before year-end, although he did not identify the project or specify a commencement date. The Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal A.V. Ndache, said: “The memorandum of understanding signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas.” The post FG moves to secure farms, attract investors appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh Domestic supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), popularly known as cooking gas, rose by 17.78 per cent year-on-year, YoY, to 4.5 million litres per day in September 2026, from 3.7 million litres per day in September 2025. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest data obtained by Vanguard. On a month-on-month, MoM, basis, supply increased by 33.33 per cent from 4.5 million litres per day in August 2026. Meanwhile, the price of cooking gas rose by 7.14 per cent to N1,400 per kg in October 2026, from N1,300 per kg in September. Reacting, former National President of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Mr. Oladapo Olatunbosun, attributed the increase to improved local production but called for sustained investment and government support to prevent shortages. He said: “Local production has increased, which is the reason for the result. However, there is much to be done by both the government and stakeholders to drive the development required to harness the potential of LPG.” Olatunbosun urged the government to encourage indigenous operators and support major domestic producers, including Dangote Petroleum Refinery, to boost output and stabilise the energy market. “The government should continue to encourage indigenous operators, and they should see it as being a partner in bringing stability to energy,” he said. He also called for affordable supplies to surrounding communities, adding that increased investment in production and distribution would improve availability. “The market is wide and large, and the more we get people investing in the production and distribution of LPG, the more available the product will be,” he said. Similarly, National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, described the supply growth as positive but stressed that consumers must benefit through improved access and affordability. “The growth in supply is a positive development because availability is fundamental to the expansion of LPG consumption. However, the real test is whether consumers are seeing improved access and more affordable prices,” he said. Obasi cautioned that increased supply would not automatically reduce retail prices, citing transportation, logistics, exchange-rate movements and other costs. He said efficient distribution was essential to ensure additional volumes reach consumers and encourage more households to switch to LPG. item.title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
item.description: The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Abdulkarim said the opposition needed to unite behind a common platform to improve its chances of defeating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the election. Speaking on Arise News, he said the coalition was already taking shape within the NDC, with Obi emerging as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him. “The opposition has to come together for us to win. The opposition have already come together. Nobody said the coalition must happen on ADC. It can happen in NDC, and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has already dropped his ambition,” he said. Abdulkarim said Atiku and other opposition figures were welcome to join the alliance to broaden its national reach. “What we are asking for is for other people to join us, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, to join all of us, so at least we will have the spread that they think they can add,” he added. The NDC campaign chief also dismissed criticism of the party’s campaign structures, arguing that its organisation should not be compared with the Obidient movement and other support groups backing Obi. “How can you compare a party with a support group? We don’t have any problem. They’re all part of the NDC party. We have more than a thousand support groups like that,” he said. On concerns about electoral fraud, Abdulkarim urged Nigerians who feared their votes might not count to support the NDC, promising that the party had developed measures to protect votes during the 2027 elections. He said the party would campaign peacefully across the country and mobilise voters who had lost confidence in the electoral process. “We are going to do our campaign peacefully. We are going to go into every corner,” he said. Abdulkarim added that the party would reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected. “I can promise anybody, anybody that feels he wants his vote to count, we have a very, very unique and serious programme that we have put in place,” he said. item.title: Ebonyi Assembly unanimously backs state police bill
item.description: The Ebonyi House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved a bill seeking to establish state police services, endorsing a constitutional amendment transmitted by the National Assembly. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that all 24 members voted in favour of the bill after extensive deliberations and consultations with their constituents. The proposed amendment seeks to alter the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to provide a legal framework for state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force at federal level. The Speaker, Moses Odunwa, said the unanimous decision demonstrated the assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the state’s security architecture. “This will also enhance access to criminal intelligence and protection of lives and properties,” Odunwa said. He described the demand for sub-national policing as a longstanding aspiration among Ebonyi residents. “The demand for a sub-national policing system has been an age-long clamour among Ebonyi people,” he said. Odunwa added that the state had formally presented its position in support of state police during a public hearing organised by the National Assembly on constitutional review. He said the bill’s passage reflected residents’ desire for a policing system closer to communities and more responsive to local security challenges. The Leader of the House, Kingsley Ikoro, said establishing state police would significantly increase manpower in the state’s security sector. Ikoro, who represents Afikpo North West under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed system would improve efforts to tackle crime at grassroots level. Other lawmakers, including Victor Nwoke (APC–Abakaliki North) and Oluchukwu Ezeali (APC–Afikpo North East), also stressed the importance of bringing policing closer to communities. They argued that decentralised policing could help address Nigeria’s security challenges by improving local responses to crime and criminal activities. Following the bill’s passage, Odunwa directed the Clerk of the House, Mrs Uche Edene, to formally transmit the assembly’s resolutions to the National Assembly. item.title: Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians
item.description: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven …As smartphone market contracts 11% amid rising device prices …Africa’s budget smartphone shipments plunge 34% amid rising costs By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s mobile market has shifted significantly towards newer network technologies over the past three years, but 5G remains out of reach for most consumers. High smartphone prices, uneven network coverage and rising infrastructure costs continue to limit adoption, despite growing demand for mobile data. In May 2023, 2G accounted for 58.36 percent of reported mobile connections, while 4G represented 25.06 percent and 5G just 0.12 percent. By August 2026, 4G had become the leading technology at 54.77 percent, while 2G fell to 36.05 percent. 5G increased to 4.92 percent. The data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, show progress but underline how slowly the newest technology is reaching the wider population. Chief Technology Officer of NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, Kingsley Uwazie, said Nigerians had a strong appetite for data consumption, but the cost of accessing 5G remained a significant barrier. “The 5G ecosystem is in its maturity phase. It has been proven that there is an appetite. Nigerians have an appetite to consume data. But there is a barrier to acquiring the devices and using the technology,” he said. High cost of compatible devices Consumers need 5G-enabled smartphones to access the technology, but rising device prices are making upgrades increasingly difficult, particularly for low-income earners. Uwazie said 5G devices remained expensive despite subsidies offered by some operators. “5G, at the moment, is not a cheap technology to deploy or to own. The cost of 5G devices has been high,” he said. He cited MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria as operators subsidising selected devices, adding that a phone available for about N50, 000 with a subsidy could cost more than N200, 000 without it. The affordability challenge has intensified as Nigeria’s smartphone market contracted by 11 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to technology research firm Omdia. Rising memory-chip costs, partly linked to growing demand from artificial intelligence, AI, data centres, have increased pressure on manufacturers and consumers. Across Africa, shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell by 34 percent year-on-year during the quarter. In Nigeria, a market assessment published by technology news platform Condia found that prices of selected Tecno, Infinix, Oppo and itel models increased between January and June 2026. The midpoint price of the itel S-Series Ultra rose from about N263, 500 to N316,400, while the Infinix Zero Series increased from approximately N550,000 to N637,500. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 28, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Continued liquidity injections by the Central Bank of Nigeria and sustained foreign currency inflows from autonomous channels have helped cushion the local currency against aggressive market pressures. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, the Naira traded around 1,341.31 to 1,352.87 per Dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day fluctuations as commercial banks and institutional buyers satisfied forex demand for import bills and capital remittances. The tight corridor underscores ongoing market clearing measures established under the refined operational framework of the central bank. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, Bureau De Change operators and street currency traders in major hubs such as Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates near 1,375 Naira per Dollar and selling rates around 1,390 Naira per Dollar. This keeps the premium between the official window and the unauthorised market relatively narrow. Financial analysts attribute the steadying market conditions to disciplined monetary policy, steady national foreign exchange reserves hovering around key operational benchmarks, and balanced seasonal demand. Market participants expect trading volumes to remain steady over the near term as both official and informal windows absorb regular commercial order flows. item.title: FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project
item.description: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m .. Tinubu says S’East must rise from potential to reality …Mbah, governors hail Tinubu, pledge support for 400km pipeline The Federal Government, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC) has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investments and create jobs in the South East. The 400-kilometre pipeline, designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. The investment agreement for the project was signed on Tuesday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu, marking a significant step towards establishing a regional gas distribution network. Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, described the project as a strategic investment that would connect the region’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states. “The Southeast’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the Southeast is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” the President said. He said the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets. “Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said. The President said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy. He, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries, industrial parks and investments that had stalled because of unreliable energy supply. “Our ambition is not simply to deliver gas to existing factories. It is to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” Tinubu said. He described the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved. item.title: PANDEF@10: Leaders push for 50% derivation
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone has called for a total overhaul of the region, demand an increase in the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 percent to 50 percent. It also wants accelerated completion of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway and urgent environmental remediation across the Niger Delta. PANDEF urged the Federal Government, the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission, RMAFC, and the National Assembly to initiate measures to raise the allocation to at least 50 percent, just as it argued that the minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. Addressing newsmen in Abuja, yesterday, after a meeting of the organisation’s Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, virtually to mark the 10 years of existence of the organisation, PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “The minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. We are demanding an upward review to 50 percent. “We also demand the abolition of the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation. We insist that offshore oil and gas operations could damage marine ecosystems and fishing grounds relied upon by coastal communities.” The meeting was attended by the Board of Trustees Chairman and former Akwa Ibom State Governor, Obong Victor Attah, former Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, Kanu Agabi, SAN, PANDEF National Publicity Secretary, Minimising Obiuwevbi, alongside political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders from the six South-South states. Further Igali said: “We propose exploring a market-based South-South investment fund to mobilise resources from individuals, businesses, institutions and other stakeholders for investment in critical sectors. The proposed fund would support enterprise development, improve regional connectivity and create jobs, with the organisation planning to engage private-sector players and other partners to develop a workable framework.” On the 2027 elections, he said: “We called on the people of the South-South to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and vote according to their conscience, choosing candidates at all levels whose programmes, commitments, and demonstrate capacity align with the aspirations of the region and who can contribute meaningfully to the peace, progress, and development of the Niger Delta. “Also as the country prepares for the elections, we are calling for a framework that extend to environmental remediation to other polluted communities. item.title: Last moments of Katsina cleric, Masussuka
item.description: Family and neighbours of the slain Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, have recalled the chain of events preceding his gruesome murder in front of his residence in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, on Monday evening. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, in an attack claimed by the extremist group Ansaru. The killing has plunged his family, followers and associates into mourning. This is as Amnesty International called on the government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. Hours before the incident, at a gathering in his father-in-law’s residence where relatives and well-wishers had assembled to mourn a deceased family member, the cleric had reportedly spoken about the inevitability of death and the need for people to live harmoniously. ‘How my 5 children died in tricycle-tanker crash’ Bangkok’s debt debate: Can Africa secure fairer development finance? Masussuka was said to have reminded the mourners that differences in race, tribe, nationality and social standing should not divide humanity because everyone would eventually return to Allah. A resident, Murtala Narega, who was familiar with the cleric’s final hours, said Masussuka used the gathering at his father-in-law’s residence to remind mourners that differences among people should encourage understanding rather than hostility. “He reminded us that Allah created people differently, but those differences should not be a reason for division or hostility,” Narega said. According to him, the cleric also spoke about the certainty of death, regardless of a person’s wealth, position, or circumstances. “He told us that this world is only a temporary place and that everyone will eventually return to Allah. He advised us to use the time we have to do good and serve humanity,” he said. Narega said the message had become particularly painful following the cleric’s death just hours later. “None of us imagined that we would be mourning him so soon after listening to him speak about death. His words have stayed with us because he reminded us that life is temporary, but we did not know that his own end was so close,” he added. After the gathering, Masussuka reportedly returned to the studio at his residence, where he regularly delivered religious lectures to his followers online. The wife of the late cleric, Hajiya Fatima, recalled that Masussuka had reminded her of the oneness of Allah before he stepped out on the fateful day, adding that shortly afterwards, she heard gunshots. “My husband spoke to me about the oneness of Allah before he left home. item.title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments. The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately. The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.” On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The statement also addressed outstanding allowances for health workers, stating that “Nineteen (19) months arrears of allowances for health workers will be redeemed within three (3) months with effect from December 2026.” On hazard allowances for agricultural workers, the ministry said the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment. On tax relief for workers, the statement said the issue would be taken to the National Executive Council because taxation is a statutory matter. The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on October 22 and came after discussions on issues raised by the NLC’s Central Working Committee and National Executive Council. item.title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition
item.description: The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them. In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing. This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu. A volunteer stands behind a banner for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP) “The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said. Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”. While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it. Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future. item.title: ‘What Are You Doing With The Money?’ Umeh Questions Tinubu’s Fresh Loan Request
item.description: The Senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, has questioned how the Federal Government has spent funds from previous borrowings, asking why budgetary obligations remain unmet despite repeated approvals for loans. Umeh spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday while reacting to President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The senator argued that previous borrowing requests were justified on the grounds that the funds would finance government budgets, yet contractors were still owed for capital projects. “The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we’ve been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day,” Umeh said. ﻿ He noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while the government had yet to meet its obligations to contractors handling capital projects. “Three budgets are running concurrently and the government is not meeting its obligations to contractors on capital projects and so on and so forth. So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question in the lips of everybody,” he said. Umeh also suggested that the latest loan request would eventually receive legislative approval, arguing that opposition lawmakers would be outvoted by members of the ruling party. President Tinubu has written to the National Assembly seeking approval for the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary external borrowing plan, valued at $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The government says the proposed loans would fund critical infrastructure, agriculture, education and other key sectors of the economy in line with the administration’s development priorities. The request has added to the debate over the government’s borrowing plans and Nigeria’s rising debt burden.
